activity.overview: Compare the same moment written as a story and as a poem.
activity.passage:
Read the same moment written two ways.

AS A STORY
Every morning, the bus came around the corner at 7:40. It was so cold that Mia could see her breath. When the bus doors opened with a hiss, warm air rushed out, and she climbed the steps and slid into her favorite seat by the window.

AS A POEM
The Morning Bus

Seven-forty, corner, cold,
my breath a little cloud.
The doors unfold, the warm air rolls,
a hiss, a sigh, out loud.

Up the steps and down the aisle,
my window seat is free.
The city stretches out a mile
and waits outside for me.

questions.prompt: The story is written in sentences and a paragraph. How is the poem written? Name two differences in how it looks on the page.
Read the poem out loud and tap the beat. Describe the rhythm. Does the story have the same kind of beat?
Which words rhyme in the poem? Why might the poet use rhyme?
Find one detail that is in both versions. How is it said differently in each?
The poem says "my breath a little cloud." What kind of figurative language is this, and what does it mean?
Which version helps you feel the moment more? Explain using an example from the text.
